category: Heat Transfer Module: Domain, Boundary, Edge and Point Features
description: Feature nodes of the Heat Transfer interfaces in COMSOL 6.4 (ht / htlsh): domain models (solid, fluid, porous, bioheat, moist, building materials), sources, thin structures (thin layer, film, fracture, thin rod), contact, phase change, periodicity, beam heating and lumped connections. Java types and property names are those used in COMSOL 6.4 Application Library models; feature tags in brackets are the default tag prefixes.

tools.name: Solid (Heat Transfer in Solids domain node)
tools.description: Default domain model of Heat Transfer in Solids that solves rho*Cp*dT/dt + rho*Cp*u_trans.grad(T) + div(q) = Q + Q_ted with q = -k grad(T), where k can be isotropic, diagonal, symmetric or full (anisotropic tensor). Properties come from the domain material or are user defined, and an optional translational velocity accounts for moving solids. Subnodes such as Phase Change Material, Irreversible Transformation, Thermoelastic Damping and Optically Thick Participating Medium extend it.
tools.usage: Heat Transfer (ht) > Solid 1 (default) or Physics toolbar > Domains > Solid. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("solid2", "SolidHeatTransferModel", 3)

parameters.name: k / k_mat
parameters.description: Thermal conductivity (from_mat or userdef, 3x3 tensor).

parameters.name: rho, Cp
parameters.description: Density and heat capacity at constant pressure (from material).

parameters.name: thermalConductivityModel
parameters.description: Standard or effective models used with subnodes.

parameters.name: coordinateSystem
parameters.description: Coordinate system for anisotropic k (e.g. a Base Vector or Curvilinear system).

tools.notes: Material frame is used for solids; with Moving Mesh or Deformed Geometry, density changes are handled automatically. For solids moving through the domain use Solid with Translational Motion.

tools.name: Fluid (Heat Transfer in Fluids domain node)
tools.description: Domain model for heat transfer in fluids with the convective term rho*Cp*u.grad(T); the velocity field and absolute pressure are model inputs taken from a flow interface (automatically with Nonisothermal Flow) or user defined. The Fluid type can be gas/liquid, ideal gas or moist air, and the heat capacity formulation can use Cp or the ratio of specific heats. Subnodes add Pressure Work, Viscous Dissipation, Phase Change Material and Convectively Enhanced Conductivity.
tools.usage: Heat Transfer in Fluids (ht) > Fluid 1 or Physics > Domains > Fluid. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("fluid2", "FluidHeatTransferModel", 3)

parameters.name: Velocity field u / Absolute pressure pA
parameters.description: User defined or e.g. 'Velocity field (spf)'.

parameters.name: Fluid type
parameters.description: Gas/liquid, Ideal gas (Rs, Cp or gamma), Moist air (InputType relativeHumidity/moistureContent/...).

parameters.name: k, rho, Cp / gamma
parameters.description: Fluid thermal properties (from_mat by default).

tools.notes: Discretization is linear by default for fluid interfaces; streamline and crosswind stabilization are active.

tools.name: Porous Medium (Heat Transfer in Porous Media domain node)
tools.description: Domain model for a porous matrix (possibly several solids) filled with a mobile fluid and optional immobile fluids. With Local thermal equilibrium one temperature with effective properties is solved; with Local thermal nonequilibrium separate fluid/solid temperatures exchange heat via q_sf = a_sf*h_sf*(Ts - Tf); with Packed bed a microscale pellet equation replaces the solid equation. Fluid and Porous Matrix subnodes hold phase properties.
tools.usage: Heat Transfer in Porous Media (ht) > Porous Medium 1 (porous1) with subnodes Fluid (fluid1) and Porous Matrix (pm1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("porous1", "PorousMediumHeatTransferModel", 3)

parameters.name: PorousMediumType
parameters.description: LocalThermalEquilibrium, LocalThermalNonequilibrium or packed bed.

parameters.name: EffectiveConductivity
parameters.description: Averaging model for k_eff (e.g. plane layers parallel/perpendicular to heat flow, power law, user defined).

parameters.name: h_sf, a_sf, d_p
parameters.description: Interstitial heat transfer coefficient, specific surface area, particle diameter (LTNE).

parameters.name: Porous Matrix: poro, k_b/k_sp, rho, Cp
parameters.description: Porosity and dry bulk or solid-phase properties.

tools.notes: Heat sources under the phase subnodes are per total volume and are weighted by the volume fraction. Thermal Dispersion and Geothermal Heating are further subnodes.

tools.name: Pellets and Pellet-Fluid Interface (Heat Transfer in Packed Beds)
tools.description: Subnodes of Porous Medium used when Porous medium type = Packed bed. Pellets defines bed porosity, pellet porosity, pellet conductivity, density and heat capacity for the microscale radial heat equation inside the pellets; Pellet-Fluid Interface defines the coupling between the pellet surface and the fluid phase (film heat transfer coefficient or temperature continuity). A Heat Source (Pellets) subnode adds reaction heat inside pellets.
tools.usage: Porous Medium > Pellets (pts1, type PelletsPorousMediumHeatTransferModel) and Porous Medium > Pellet-Fluid Interface (pfi1, type PelletFluidInterfacePorousMediumHeatTransferModel).

parameters.name: poro, poro_pe
parameters.description: Bed porosity and pellet (intraparticle) porosity.

parameters.name: k_pe, rho_pe, Cp_pe
parameters.description: Pellet thermal conductivity, density, heat capacity.

parameters.name: Pellet-fluid coupling
parameters.description: Heat transfer coefficient h_pf (e.g. from correlation) or continuity.

tools.example:
ht > Porous Medium 1: Porous medium type = Packed bed
Pellets 1: poro = 0.4, pellet radius 1.5[mm], k_pe = 0.3[W/(m*K)]
Pellet-Fluid Interface 1: film heat transfer coefficient
Heat Source (Pellets): Q = -dH_r*r_rate
tools.notes: Radiation is only handled on the outer surfaces of the pellets. See also the Pellet material subnode of Porous Material.

tools.name: Immobile Fluids (Heat Transfer in Porous Media)
tools.description: Subnode of Porous Medium (and of Porous Matrix) that accounts for fluids trapped in the pores (ice, stagnant water, air pockets) in the effective volumetric heat capacity and conductivity. Each immobile fluid has a volume fraction theta_imf and its own k, rho and Cp; the volume fractions can come from a Porous Material with Immobile Fluid subnodes.
tools.usage: Porous Medium > Immobile Fluids (imf1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").feature("porous1").create("imf1", "ImmobileFluidPorousMaterial", 2)

parameters.name: theta_imf
parameters.description: Volume fraction of the immobile fluid (from material or user).

parameters.name: k_imf, rho_imf, Cp_imf
parameters.description: Thermal properties of the immobile fluid.

parameters.name: Phase change
parameters.description: Combine with Phase Change Material for freezing/thawing of pore water.

tools.notes: Immobile fluid properties can be defined in the Immobile Fluid subnode of a Porous Material (material type ImFluid).

tools.name: Thermal Dispersion (Heat Transfer in Porous Media)
tools.description: Subnode that models hydrodynamic mixing of the fluid flowing through a porous medium by adding a dispersive conductivity k_disp to k_eff, computed from the Darcy velocity and longitudinal and transverse dispersivities (fourth-order dispersivity tensor). Important for groundwater heat transport, aquifer thermal storage and packed-bed reactors with significant pore velocity.
tools.usage: Porous Medium > Thermal Dispersion (right-click Porous Medium).

parameters.name: Longitudinal dispersivity lambda_lo
parameters.description: Dispersivity along the flow direction.

parameters.name: Transverse dispersivity
parameters.description: Isotropic lambda_tr, or separate horizontal/vertical values in 3D (z vertical).

tools.example:
ht > Porous Medium 1 > Thermal Dispersion 1
Longitudinal dispersivity = 5[m], Transverse dispersivity = 0.5[m]
Fluid velocity from Darcy's Law (dl)
tools.notes: In 1D only the longitudinal dispersivity is used; in 2D and 2D axisymmetric one transverse value.

tools.name: Geothermal Heating (Heat Transfer in Porous Media)
tools.description: Porous Medium subnode that adds radiogenic heat production Q_geo = rho_geo*q_geo*f(z_geo) to the heat equation. The distribution is uniform or exponential with depth, f = exp(z_geo/h_geo), and the geothermal density can be based on solids, on all porous-media components or user defined. Requires the Subsurface Flow Module (or Porous Media Flow Module).
tools.usage: Porous Medium > Geothermal Heating

parameters.name: q_geo
parameters.description: Radiogenic heating per unit mass (W/kg).

parameters.name: Distribution type
parameters.description: Uniform or Exponential (length scale h_geo, depth z_geo).

parameters.name: Geothermal density
parameters.description: Solids, Porous media or User defined rho_geo.

tools.example:
ht > Porous Medium 1 > Geothermal Heating 1
q_geo = 1e-9[W/kg], Exponential, h_geo = 10[km], z_geo = -z
Combined with a basal Heat Flux of 0.06[W/m^2] for a crustal temperature profile
tools.notes: Maximum source where z_geo = 0 (typically the top surface).

tools.name: Bioheat (Bioheat Transfer, Pennes perfusion source)
tools.description: Subnode of Biological Tissue implementing the Pennes bioheat source rho_b*C_p,b*omega_b*(T_b - T) + Q_met: blood perfusion with arterial blood temperature, blood density, heat capacity and perfusion rate, plus metabolic heat generation. Used in hyperthermia, ablation and cryotherapy models.
tools.usage: Bioheat Transfer (ht) > Biological Tissue > Bioheat (bh1). Parameters via model.component("comp1").physics("ht").feature("bt1").feature("bh1").set(...)

parameters.name: Tb
parameters.description: Arterial blood temperature (310.15 K default).

parameters.name: Cp_b, rhobl
parameters.description: Specific heat and density of blood.

parameters.name: omegab
parameters.description: Blood perfusion rate (1/s).

parameters.name: Qmet
parameters.description: Metabolic heat source (W/m^3).

tools.notes: Perfusion can be made damage-dependent, e.g. omegab*(1 - ht.theta_d).

tools.name: Biological Tissue (Bioheat Transfer)
tools.description: Default domain node of the Bioheat Transfer interface that solves the bioheat equation in tissue with conductivity, density and heat capacity from the tissue material (e.g. Bioheat material library: liver, muscle, fat, bone, lung, myocardium, prostate, skin). Perfusion and metabolism are added with a Bioheat subnode and tissue necrosis or freezing damage with a Thermal Damage subnode.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Bioheat Transfer; default node Biological Tissue 1 (bt1). Interface Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("ht", "BioHeat", "geom1")

parameters.name: k, rho, Cp
parameters.description: Tissue properties (from material).

parameters.name: Volume reference temperature
parameters.description: For temperature-dependent density on the material frame.

parameters.name: Subnodes
parameters.description: Bioheat (bh), Thermal Damage (tdam).

tools.notes: Bioheat materials include Arrhenius frequency factor and activation energy for some tissues (e.g. liver 7.39e39 1/s, 2.577e5 J/mol).

tools.name: Thermal Damage (Bioheat Transfer)
tools.description: Biological Tissue subnode that computes tissue damage from overheating or freezing. The Temperature threshold model accumulates damage time above a damage temperature (hyperthermia) or below one (cryogenic) with instant necrosis beyond a necrosis temperature; the Arrhenius kinetics model integrates d(alpha)/dt = A*exp(-dE/(R*T))*(1-alpha)^n (hyperthermia only). Damaged-tissue properties and an enthalpy change can be specified.
tools.usage: Biological Tissue > Thermal Damage (tdam1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").feature("bt1").create("tdam1", "ThermalDamage", 2)

parameters.name: TransformationModel
parameters.description: Temperature threshold, ArrheniusKinetics or user defined.

parameters.name: T_dh, t_dh, T_nh
parameters.description: Hyperthermia damage temperature (323.15 K), damage time (50 s), necrosis temperature (373.15 K).

parameters.name: A, deltaE, n
parameters.description: Arrhenius frequency factor, activation energy, polynomial order (from material).

parameters.name: SpecifyDiffMatProps, k_d, rho_d
parameters.description: Properties of the damaged tissue.

tools.notes: Variables ht.theta_d, ht.alpha and ht.alphanecr are available for plots of lesion size.

tools.name: Irreversible Transformation (Heat Transfer in Solids)
tools.description: Solid subnode for thermally induced irreversible transformations of non-biological solids (curing, charring, thermal decomposition, food cooking). The transformation fraction theta_it follows a Temperature threshold model (overheating or overcooling with transformation temperature and time), Arrhenius kinetics (frequency factor, activation energy, order n) or a user-defined expression; the associated enthalpy change adds a heat source and properties can switch to a transformed material.
tools.usage: Heat Transfer in Solids > Solid > Irreversible Transformation (right-click Solid).

parameters.name: Transformation model
parameters.description: Temperature threshold (default), Arrhenius kinetics, User defined.

parameters.name: T_it,h / t_it,h / L_it,h
parameters.description: Transformation temperature, time and enthalpy change for overheating (analogous for overcooling).

parameters.name: A, dE, n, L
parameters.description: Arrhenius parameters and enthalpy change.

parameters.name: Specify different material properties for the transformed state
parameters.description: Transformed material with its own k, rho, Cp.

tools.example:
ht > Solid 1 > Irreversible Transformation 1
Transformation model: Arrhenius kinetics, A = 1e12[1/s], dE = 150[kJ/mol], n = 1
Transformed material: 'Charred wood'
Study: Time Dependent fire-exposure test
tools.notes: The biological-tissue counterpart is Thermal Damage (Bioheat Transfer).

tools.name: Building Material (Heat Transfer in Building Materials)
tools.description: Domain node modeling a building material as a porous medium containing liquid water and vapor: effective volumetric heat capacity and effective conductivity depend on moisture content, and the latent heat of evaporation adds the term div(Lv*delta_p*grad(phi_w*p_sat)). Moisture content and relative humidity come from the Moisture Transport interface via the Heat and Moisture coupling.
tools.usage: Heat Transfer in Building Materials (ht) > Building Material 1 (bm1), type BuildingMaterialHeatTransferModel.

parameters.name: ThermalConductivityType
parameters.description: Equivalent thermal conductivity (moisture dependent) or from solid conductivity and moisture correction factor b.

parameters.name: rhos, Cps
parameters.description: Dry solid density and heat capacity.

parameters.name: wc
parameters.description: Moisture content (from mt or material storage function).

parameters.name: delta_p / mu_vrf
parameters.description: Vapor permeability or vapor resistance factor (MaterialType).

tools.notes: Second-order temperature discretization by default in this interface.

tools.name: Moist Air (Heat Transfer in Moist Air domain node)
tools.description: Domain node for convection and diffusion in moist air with rho, Cp and k evaluated from the amount of vapor, specified as relative humidity, vapor concentration, moisture content (humidity ratio) or vapor mass fraction, typically from a Moisture Transport in Air interface. Saturation indicators (ht.satInd) show where condensation can occur.
tools.usage: Heat Transfer in Moist Air (ht) > Moist Air 1 (ma1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("ma1", "MoistAirHeatTransferModel", 2)

parameters.name: InputType
parameters.description: relativeHumidity, vapor concentration, moistureContent (xvap) or vapor mass fraction.

parameters.name: Velocity field / Absolute pressure
parameters.description: From flow interface or user defined.

parameters.name: Condition checks
parameters.description: Reference conditions for saturation (T_cond, p_cond, phi_cond).

tools.notes: Moist-air variables: ht.phi (relative humidity), ht.T_dp (dew point), ht.psat, ht.xvap, ht.satInd.

tools.name: Moist Porous Medium (Heat Transfer in Moist Porous Media)
tools.description: Domain node for heat transfer in a porous matrix filled with moist air and liquid water, with effective volumetric heat capacity rho*Cp_eff = theta_s*rho_s*Cp_s + eps_p*(s_l*rho_l*Cp_l + (1-s_l)*rho_g*Cp_g) and Darcy velocities of gas and liquid. With the Heat and Moisture coupling, the evaporation source Q_evap and the enthalpy fluxes are taken from the moisture equation.
tools.usage: ht > Moist Porous Medium (mporous1) with subnodes Porous Matrix, Liquid Water, Moist Air. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("mporous1", "MoistPorousMediumHeatTransferModel", 2)

parameters.name: Porous Matrix
parameters.description: Dry bulk or solid-phase conductivity, density and heat capacity; porosity.

parameters.name: Liquid Water / Moist Air
parameters.description: Phase velocities (u_l, u_g) and properties.

parameters.name: Effective conductivity
parameters.description: Averaging model.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("mporous1", "MoistPorousMediumHeatTransferModel", 2);
// Application Library: Heat_Transfer_Module/Phase_Change/potato_drying
tools.notes: Pair with Hygroscopic Porous Medium in the Moisture Transport interface on the same domains.

tools.name: Convectively Enhanced Conductivity (Heat Transfer in Fluids)
tools.description: Fluid or Moist Air subnode that replaces explicit natural convection in closed cavities by multiplying the fluid conductivity with a Nusselt number from a correlation (Horizontal cavity heated from below, Vertical rectangular cavity) or a user value, and sets the fluid velocity to zero. It gives fast estimates for air gaps without solving a flow field.
tools.usage: Fluid > Convectively Enhanced Conductivity. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").feature("fluid1").create("cec1", "ConvectivelyEnhancedConductivity", 3)

parameters.name: Nusselt number correlation
parameters.description: Horizontal cavity heated from below (H, dT), Vertical rectangular cavity (H, L, dT), User defined Nu.

parameters.name: Temperature difference
parameters.description: Automatic (max - min on exterior boundaries) or user defined.

parameters.name: Dynamic viscosity
parameters.description: Needed except for moist air.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("ht").feature("fluid1").create("cec1", "ConvectivelyEnhancedConductivity", 3);
// Application Library: Heat_Transfer_Module/Phase_Change/evaporative_cooling
tools.notes: For moist air, natural convection due to vapor concentration gradients is neglected.

tools.name: Pressure Work and Viscous Dissipation (Heat Transfer in Fluids)
tools.description: Fluid subnodes adding mechanical energy terms to the heat equation: Pressure Work adds alpha_p*T*(dp/dt + u.grad(p)) (adiabatic compression and thermoacoustic effects), Viscous Dissipation adds tau:grad(u) (and Darcy/Forchheimer drag terms in porous media). Both are overridden by the Nonisothermal Flow coupling when that coupling includes them.
tools.usage: Fluid > Pressure Work / Viscous Dissipation. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").feature("fluid1").create("pw1", "PressureWork", 2)

parameters.name: Pressure Work
parameters.description: No settings; uses coefficient of thermal expansion alpha_p of the fluid.

parameters.name: Viscous Dissipation Q_vd
parameters.description: User defined or from the fluid flow interface.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("ht").feature("fluid1").create("pw1", "PressureWork", 2);
// Application Library: Multibody_Dynamics_Module/Automotive_and_Aerospace/reciprocating_engine
tools.notes: Viscous Dissipation was previously called Viscous Heating. Pressure work is small at low Mach numbers.

tools.name: Solid with Translational Motion (Heat Transfer in Solids)
tools.description: Domain node like Solid but solved on the spatial frame with a Translational Motion subnode that adds the convective term rho*Cp*u_trans.grad(T) for rectilinear scrolling or rotating solids (continuous casting strands, rotating brake discs, rolling, welding with moving source frame). It avoids a moving mesh when the geometry is invariant along the motion.
tools.usage: Physics > Domains > Solid with Translational Motion (solidtrm1) with subnode Translational Motion (trm1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("solidtrm1", "SolidWithTranslationalMotion", 3)

parameters.name: u (Translational Motion)
parameters.description: Velocity vector, e.g. (0,0,v_cast) or rotational -Omega*y, Omega*x.

parameters.name: k, rho, Cp
parameters.description: Solid properties.

parameters.name: Stabilization
parameters.description: Streamline/crosswind diffusion for high Peclet numbers.

tools.notes: Cannot be combined with a Moving Mesh node on the same domain; COMSOL recommends Solid + Moving Mesh when the solid also deforms.

tools.name: Cell Periodicity (Heat Transfer in Solids, thermal homogenization)
tools.description: Domain node for representative volume elements (RVE) or repeating unit cells of periodic microstructures: it imposes periodic temperature (with Boundary Pair subnodes on opposite faces) or uniform temperature gradient conditions and computes the homogenized conductivity tensor, heat capacity and density. The results can be turned into a new homogenized material through Load Group, Material and Study Generation.
tools.usage: Heat Transfer in Solids > Cell Periodicity (cp1) with Boundary Pair subnodes. Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("cp1", "CellPeriodicity", 3)

parameters.name: BoundaryConditions
parameters.description: Periodic temperature (ManualPeriodic) or Uniform temperature gradient.

parameters.name: lambdaT
parameters.description: Temperature scale factor (amplitude of the imposed temperature differences).

parameters.name: Create material / study
parameters.description: Generates load groups, a study and a homogenized material.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("cp1", "CellPeriodicity", 3);
// Application Library: Heat_Transfer_Module/Applications/equivalent_properties_of_periodic_microstructures
tools.notes: Only applicable on Solid domains (conduction). The structural counterpart creates Cell Periodicity in Solid Mechanics.

tools.name: Optically Thick Participating Medium (Heat Transfer, Rosseland approximation)
tools.description: Solid/Fluid subnode implementing the Rosseland approximation for radiation in optically thick media: radiation is represented by an added conductivity k_R = 16*n_r^2*sigma*T^3/(3*beta_R), so no radiative intensity is solved. Use it for glass at high temperature, ceramics, insulation fibers and dense particle clouds where the optical thickness is large.
tools.usage: Solid or Fluid > Optically Thick Participating Medium (otpm1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").feature("solid1").create("otpm1", "OpticallyThickParticipatingMedium", 3)

parameters.name: nrad
parameters.description: Refractive index n_r (1 approximates air).

parameters.name: SpecifyMediaProperties
parameters.description: Absorption and scattering coefficients (kappa_R, sigma_S) or Rosseland mean extinction coefficient beta_R directly.

tools.example:
model.component("comp3").physics("ht3").feature("solid1").create("otpm1", "OpticallyThickParticipatingMedium", 3);
// Application Library: Heat_Transfer_Module/Thermal_Radiation/glass_plate (compared against DOM and P1)
tools.notes: Inaccurate near boundaries and for optically thin media; use Radiation in Participating Media there.

tools.name: Heat Source (Heat Transfer in Solids and Fluids)
tools.description: Domain source Q in the heat equation, given as a General source Q0 (W/m^3), a Linear source q_s*T (accounted for in stabilization), or a total Heat rate P0 spread over the selection volume. With other physics present, predefined General-source options appear: Total power dissipation density (ec), Total power dissipation density / Electromagnetic power loss density (emw), Electromagnetic heating (mf). Sources can be marked as harmonic perturbations for frequency-domain thermal studies.
tools.usage: Physics > Domains > Heat Source (hs1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("hs1", "HeatSource", 3)

parameters.name: heatSourceType
parameters.description: GeneralSource, LinearSource or HeatRate.

parameters.name: Q0 / Q0_src
parameters.description: Source density, user defined or predefined from another interface.

parameters.name: qs, P0
parameters.description: Production/absorption coefficient; total heat rate.

parameters.name: materialType
parameters.description: Solid (material frame) or Nonsolid (spatial frame).

tools.notes: Positive values heat, negative cool. Results variable ht.Qtot and global ht.QInt. Prefer the Electromagnetic Heating coupling over predefined sources for two-way coupling.

tools.name: Battery Layers (Heat Transfer, homogenized battery cells)
tools.description: 3D domain node (Battery Design Module license) modeling heat transfer in wound or stacked battery cells without resolving individual layers: anisotropic conductivity with in-layer and through-layer values in a Cartesian (flat parallel / pouch) or cylindrical (spirally wound) configuration, plus effective density and heat capacity. Combine with a heat source from a lumped or detailed battery model.
tools.usage: Physics > Domains > Battery Layers (bl1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("bl1", "BatteryLayers", 3)

parameters.name: LayerConfiguration
parameters.description: SpirallyWound (cylindrical) or flat parallel (pouch/prismatic).

parameters.name: LongitudinalAxis / ThroughLayerDirection
parameters.description: Cylinder axis or layer normal (x, y or z axis).

parameters.name: InLayerConductivity, ThroughLayerConductivity, Density, HeatCapacity
parameters.description: Effective cell properties.

tools.notes: Rectangular Block Selection and Semicylinder Selection helpers assist in selecting cell regions.

tools.name: Thermoelastic Damping and Shape Memory Alloy (Heat Transfer in Solids)
tools.description: Thermoelastic Damping is a Solid subnode adding the heat source Q_ted = -alpha*T*dS/dt from stress changes (user defined or from the solid mechanics Thermal Expansion subnode) - important for MEMS resonators and high-frequency vibration. Shape Memory Alloy is a domain node whose conductivity and heat capacity follow the martensite/austenite composition computed by the structural Shape Memory Alloy material model, including the latent heat of the phase transformation.
tools.usage: Solid > Thermoelastic Damping; Physics > Domains > Shape Memory Alloy (heat transfer).

parameters.name: Q_ted
parameters.description: Thermoelastic damping source, user defined or from solid mechanics.

parameters.name: SMA properties
parameters.description: Phase-dependent k and Cp (material groups ShapeMemoryAlloyAustenite / ShapeMemoryAlloyMartensite).

tools.example:
Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material > Thermal Expansion + Heat Transfer in Solids > Solid > Thermoelastic Damping (from solid mechanics)
Study: Eigenfrequency to get the thermoelastic Q factor of a MEMS beam
tools.notes: Shape Memory Alloy (heat) is designed to be coupled with the Shape Memory Alloy feature of Solid Mechanics (Nonlinear Structural Materials Module).

tools.name: Out-of-Plane Heat Flux and Out-of-Plane Radiation (Heat Transfer)
tools.description: Domain nodes for 1D and 2D models that add heat exchange through the out-of-plane faces of thin or slender objects: Out-of-Plane Heat Flux applies upside and downside fluxes (general, convective with correlations, or nucleate boiling), Out-of-Plane Radiation adds surface-to-ambient radiation from both faces. With the Thickness node (2D) or cross-section settings (1D) they reduce 3D plates and rods to lower dimension.
tools.usage: Physics > Domains > Out-of-Plane Heat Flux (ophf1) / Out-of-Plane Radiation (oprd1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("ophf1", "OutOfPlaneHeatFlux", 2); ...create("oprd1", "OutOfPlaneRadiation", 2)

parameters.name: Upside / Downside inward heat flux
parameters.description: Flux type and h, Text for each side.

parameters.name: Surface emissivity, ambient temperature
parameters.description: For Out-of-Plane Radiation (up and down).

parameters.name: Thickness dz
parameters.description: From the interface or a Thickness node.

tools.notes: Disabled when a radiation multiphysics coupling is active on the same domain (infinite out-of-plane assumption). Variables ht.tflux_u, ht.q0_u etc.

tools.name: Heat Flux (Heat Transfer in Solids and Fluids)
tools.description: Boundary condition adding an inward heat flux q0 (positive heats the domain). Flux types: General inward heat flux; Convective heat flux h*(Text - T) with h user defined or from built-in correlations for external/internal natural and forced convection using air, transformer oil, water, moist air or a material; Heat rate P0 divided over the boundary area; and Nucleate boiling heat flux (Rohsenow). External temperature and pressure can come from Ambient Properties.
tools.usage: Physics > Boundaries > Heat Flux (hf1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("hf1", "HeatFluxBoundary", 2)

parameters.name: HeatFluxType
parameters.description: GeneralInwardHeatFlux (q0_input), ConvectiveHeatFlux, HeatRate (P0), nucleate boiling.

parameters.name: HeatTransferCoefficientType
parameters.description: UserDef (h), ExtNaturalConvection, IntNaturalConvection, ExtForcedConvection, IntForcedConvection.

parameters.name: ExtNaturalConvectionType / ExtForcedConvectionType
parameters.description: VerticalWall, HorizontalPlateUp, ... / PlateAveragedTransferCoefficient, PlateLocalTransferCoefficient, ... with Lwall, Lpl, U, D.

parameters.name: Text, pA, ExternalFluidType
parameters.description: External temperature, absolute pressure, fluid (Air default).

tools.notes: Not for inlet boundaries (use Inflow). With a Radiation Shield in an S2S coupling, the flux acts on the outermost shield temperature. Variable ht.hf1.h gives the evaluated coefficient.

tools.name: Temperature (Heat Transfer in Solids and Fluids)
tools.description: Dirichlet condition T = T0 on boundaries (also edges and points), with T0 constant, an expression, a function of time or an Ambient temperature from Ambient Properties. Constraint settings allow pointwise, weak or Nitsche constraints, and a Harmonic Perturbation subnode defines a temperature amplitude for frequency-domain thermal perturbation studies.
tools.usage: Physics > Boundaries > Temperature (temp1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("temp1", "TemperatureBoundary", 2)

parameters.name: T0 / T0_src
parameters.description: Prescribed temperature (userdef or ambient temperature).

parameters.name: constraintOptions
parameters.description: pointwiseConstraints (default), weak or Nitsche constraints.

parameters.name: Harmonic Perturbation subnode
parameters.description: Temperature perturbation Delta T0.

tools.notes: At flow inlets prefer Inflow (Danckwerts) when upstream diffusion matters. Reaction flux is available as ht.ntflux on constrained boundaries.

tools.name: Inflow (Heat Transfer in Fluids)
tools.description: Inlet condition for nonsolid domains that models inflow through a virtual upstream domain with a Danckwerts condition on the sensible enthalpy: the upstream temperature T_ustr (and optionally upstream absolute pressure) is known, but the inlet temperature is not strictly enforced, so heat sources or constraints near the inlet produce a physically consistent profile. At high flow rates it approaches a Temperature condition.
tools.usage: Physics > Boundaries > Inflow (ifl1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("ifl1", "Inflow", 2)

parameters.name: Tustr / Tustr_src
parameters.description: Upstream temperature (user defined or ambient temperature).

parameters.name: specifyUpstreamAbsolutePressure / pustr
parameters.description: Account for pressure work between upstream and inlet.

tools.notes: See 'Choosing Between the Temperature and the Inflow Conditions' in the Heat Transfer Module User's Guide.

tools.name: Periodic Condition (Heat Transfer)
tools.description: Boundary condition that makes temperature periodic between source and destination boundaries, optionally with a temperature offset Delta_T (T_dst = T_src + Delta_T). Destination selection and orientation can be set explicitly; constraints default to Nitsche. Use it for repeating fin arrays, periodic channels and unit cells.
tools.usage: Physics > Boundaries > Periodic Condition (pc1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("pc1", "PeriodicHeat", 2)

parameters.name: DeltaT
parameters.description: Temperature offset between source and destination (0 K default).

parameters.name: constraintOptions
parameters.description: nitscheConstraints (default), pointwise or weak.

parameters.name: Orientation of Source / Destination
parameters.description: Mapping for non-matching orientations.

tools.notes: Combine with Periodic Flow Condition in the flow interface for periodic conjugate heat transfer.

tools.name: Deposited Beam Power (Heat Transfer, laser and electron beams)
tools.description: Boundary heat source for narrow beams (laser, electron beam, welding torch) hitting a surface: the deposited power P0 is distributed with a built-in Gaussian (standard deviation sigma) or top-hat disk (radius R, optional smoothing) profile around a beam origin O along an orientation e, or a user-defined beam power density I0. Moving the origin with time (e.g. O = (v*t, 0, 0)) models scanning lasers and welding paths.
tools.usage: Physics > Boundaries > Deposited Beam Power (dbp1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("dbp1", "DepositedBeamPower", 2)

parameters.name: e
parameters.description: Beam orientation vector.

parameters.name: beamProfile
parameters.description: builtInProfiles or user defined I0.

parameters.name: DistributionType, sigma, radius, dradius
parameters.description: Gaussian or top-hat disk parameters.

parameters.name: P0, O
parameters.description: Deposited beam power and beam origin point.

parameters.name: SourcePosition
parameters.description: Layer, Upside or Downside (advanced).

tools.notes: Refine the mesh at the spot; if sigma or R is smaller than the mesh, COMSOL substitutes a minimum length. For volumetric absorption in semitransparent media use Radiative Beam in Absorbing Media.

tools.name: Thin Layer (Heat Transfer in Solids)
tools.description: Boundary node representing a thin solid layer (coating, glue, oxide, foil, multilayer stack) on interior or exterior boundaries without meshing it. Layer type Thermally thick approximation neglects tangential conduction (resistive layer, multiple sublayers allowed), Thermally thin approximation neglects the through-thickness gradient (conductive sheet), and General solves both directions on the extra-dimension product space. Thickness comes from a Single Layer Material, Layered Material Link/Stack or a user value.
tools.usage: Physics > Boundaries > Thin Layer (sls1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("sls1", "SolidLayeredShell", 2)

parameters.name: LayerType
parameters.description: Resistive (thermally thick approximation), Conductive (thermally thin approximation) or General.

parameters.name: lth / lth_mat
parameters.description: Layer thickness (user defined or from the layered material).

parameters.name: k, rho, Cp
parameters.description: Layer properties (from material or user defined).

parameters.name: ThermalResistanceType / R_s
parameters.description: Specify the layer by thermal resistance instead of properties.

tools.notes: Upside/downside temperatures are ht.Tu / ht.Td; use Heat Source (Thin Layer) for sources in selected sublayers and External Temperature to fix the exterior side.

tools.name: Thin Film (Heat Transfer in Fluids)
tools.description: Boundary node behaving like the Fluid domain model on boundaries: it represents a thin fluid layer (lubricant film, thin air gap, liquid film) with in-plane convection and conduction, using the same layer types (thermally thin, general) and layered-material thickness definitions as Thin Layer. It is the in-domain counterpart of the Heat Transfer in Films interface.
tools.usage: Physics > Boundaries > Thin Film (fls1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("fls1", "FluidLayeredShell", 2)

parameters.name: LayerType
parameters.description: ThermallyThinApproximation or General.

parameters.name: Film velocity
parameters.description: Tangential velocity field of the film.

parameters.name: Fluid properties
parameters.description: k, rho, Cp (or moist-air input types).

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("fls1", "FluidLayeredShell", 2);
// Application Library: Heat_Transfer_Module/Medical_Technology/isothermal_box
tools.notes: Restrict to layered boundaries to apply only where a layered material exists.

tools.name: Fracture (Heat Transfer in Porous Media)
tools.description: Boundary node for heat transfer in fractures (thin porous layers) inside porous or solid domains: porous-media averaged conduction and convection along the fracture, using a layered material for the aperture and a velocity typically from the Fracture Flow feature of Darcy's Law. Layer types match Thin Layer.
tools.usage: Physics > Boundaries > Fracture (pmls1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("pmls1", "PorousMediumLayeredShell", 2)

parameters.name: theta_p
parameters.description: Fracture porosity/volume fraction (e.g. root.comp1.dl.theta).

parameters.name: k_p, rho_p, Cp_p
parameters.description: Porous matrix properties in the fracture.

parameters.name: EffectiveConductivity
parameters.description: Averaging model.

parameters.name: LayerType
parameters.description: Thermally thin approximation or General.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("pmls1", "PorousMediumLayeredShell", 2);
// Application Library: Subsurface_Flow_Module/Heat_Transfer/geothermal_doublet
tools.notes: Can also represent heat transfer in films. Stand-alone boundary interface: Heat Transfer in Fractures (htlsh).

tools.name: External Temperature (Thin Layer, Thin Film, Fracture)
tools.description: Subnode of Thin Layer, Thin Film or Fracture that prescribes the temperature T0 on the exterior side of the layer (user value or ambient temperature), with pointwise or weak constraints. With a thermally thin layer it is equivalent to a Temperature condition; a Harmonic Perturbation subnode allows frequency-domain perturbation studies.
tools.usage: Thin Layer (sls1) > External Temperature (right-click the thin-structure node).

parameters.name: T0
parameters.description: External-side temperature (user defined or ambient).

parameters.name: Constraint settings
parameters.description: Pointwise (default) or weak constraints.

tools.example: ht > Thin Layer 1 (exterior insulation board, thermally thick) > External Temperature 1: T0 = ampr1.T_amb
tools.notes: Use Heat Flux on the layer for convective exterior conditions instead.

tools.name: Heat Source (Thin Layer, Thin Film, Fracture)
tools.description: Subnode that adds an internal heat source Q_s inside a thin layer, film or fracture; with layered materials the contribution can be limited to selected layers (clear Use all layers), so for example only the resistive trace of a heater stack or one ply of a laminate is heated.
tools.usage: Thin Layer > Heat Source (right-click the thin-structure node); layer selection in Shell Properties.

parameters.name: Q_s
parameters.description: Heat source per unit volume (or total) of the selected layers.

parameters.name: Use all layers / layer checkboxes
parameters.description: Restrict to individual layers of a Layered Material Link/Stack or Single Layer Material.

tools.example:
ht > Thin Layer 1 (Layered Material Link: Cu/FR4/Cu, General) > Heat Source 1
Clear 'Use all layers', select only the top copper layer, Q_s = P_trace/V_trace
tools.notes: Sublayers are distinguished only for Thermally thick approximation and General layer types.

tools.name: Thermal Contact (Heat Transfer in Solids)
tools.description: Interior-boundary or pair condition for imperfect contact between two solids: heat flux -n.q = h*(T_u - T_d) with joint conductance h = h_c + h_g + h_r. Contact model Constriction conductance with interstitial gas uses Cooper-Mikic-Yovanovich (plastic, with microhardness, Vickers or Brinell hardness) or Mikic elastic correlations from asperity height/slope and contact pressure plus a parallel-plate gap conductance; Equivalent thin resistive layer uses a layer resistance, conductance or conductivity/thickness. Radiative conductance (gray-diffuse parallel surfaces) matters above about 600 degC; friction heat can be added as a boundary source.
tools.usage: Physics > Boundaries > Thin Structures > Thermal Contact (tc1), or Pairs > Thermal Contact (ptc1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("tc1", "ThermalContact", 2); pair: create("ptc1", "PairThermalContact", 2)

parameters.name: ContactModel
parameters.description: ConstrictionConductance or EquThinLayer.

parameters.name: hcType / hgType / hrType
parameters.description: CMY (Cooper-Mikic-Yovanovich), Mikic elastic or user; gap: UserDef or PPG (parallel-plate gas); radiative: UserDef or gray-diffuse.

parameters.name: sigma_asp, m_asp, Tn (contact pressure)
parameters.description: Asperity height, slope and contact pressure (from structural contact in pair mode).

parameters.name: hardnessList, Hmic / Hvick / Hbrin
parameters.description: Hardness definition for CMY.

parameters.name: Specify, Req, heq, ds
parameters.description: Equivalent thin layer resistance/conductance/thickness.

tools.notes: Results: ht.tc1.hconstr, ht.tc1.hgap, ht.tc1.hjoint, ht.tc1.Qb. The pair version must sit on an Identity Pair or a structural Contact Pair.

tools.name: Phase Change Interface (Heat Transfer in Solids and Fluids, Stefan condition)
tools.description: Boundary condition that tracks a sharp melting/solidification front with the Stefan condition: the interface temperature is fixed to the phase change temperature T_pc and the jump in normal heat flux equals rho*L*v_n, which drives a moving mesh (Deformed Geometry/Moving Mesh) to move the front. Applicable between Fluid and Solid domains or inside Solid, Fluid and Porous Medium domains in 2D, 2D axisymmetric and 3D; the coldest phase must be immobile and topology changes are not allowed. Phase Change Interface, Exterior handles exterior boundaries (e.g. ablation).
tools.usage: Physics > Boundaries > Phase Change Interface (pci1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("pci1", "PhaseChangeInterface", 1)

parameters.name: Tpc
parameters.description: Phase change temperature.

parameters.name: L
parameters.description: Latent heat of phase change.

parameters.name: SolidSideType
parameters.description: Which side (Upside/Downside) is the solid phase.

parameters.name: rho_s, rho_f, us
parameters.description: Phase densities and solid velocity.

parameters.name: HeatFluxJumpEvaluationType
parameters.description: LagrangeMultiplier (default) evaluation of the flux jump.

tools.notes: Front velocity variable ht.pci1.vn. When topology changes are expected use Phase Change Material (apparent heat capacity) instead.

tools.name: Isothermal Domain Interface (Heat Transfer)
tools.description: Boundary node that defines how an Isothermal Domain (lumped single-temperature domain) exchanges heat with its neighbors: Thermal insulation (default), Continuity, Ventilation (mass flux between fluid domains), Convective heat flux (with the same correlations as Heat Flux), Nucleate boiling heat flux, or Thermal contact (surface or total thermal resistance). A default instance is created with each Isothermal Domain.
tools.usage: Physics > Boundaries > Isothermal Domain Interface (idi1); requires an Isothermal Domain (id1, type IsothermalDomain).

parameters.name: InterfaceType
parameters.description: ThermalInsulation, Continuity, Ventilation, ConvectiveHeatFlux, NucleateBoiling, ThermalContact.

parameters.name: mfPlus / mrPlus ...
parameters.description: Ventilation mass flux or mass flow rate in the chosen flow direction.

parameters.name: h, HeatTransferCoefficientType
parameters.description: Convective coefficient or correlation.

parameters.name: Rt_s / Rt
parameters.description: Surface or total thermal resistance for thermal contact.

tools.notes: Cannot be applied on boundaries inside a single isothermal domain. Isothermal domain temperature is available as ht.id1.T.

tools.name: Local Thermal Nonequilibrium Boundary (Heat Transfer in Porous Media)
tools.description: Default node active on all boundaries adjacent to Porous Medium domains with Local thermal nonequilibrium; it shows where two temperatures Tf and Ts are solved and blocks single-temperature conditions there. Exceptions are thin-structure nodes (Thin Layer, Thin Film, Fracture, Thermal Contact), Thermal Insulation and Periodic Condition; other conditions must be added as subnodes of the Fluid or Porous Matrix subnodes.
tools.usage: Automatically present (ltneb1) in Local Thermal Nonequilibrium models; add phase-specific conditions via Porous Medium > Fluid / Porous Matrix > right-click.

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Read-only list of two-temperature boundaries.

parameters.name: Phase-specific subnodes
parameters.description: Temperature, Heat Flux, Inflow, Outflow, Continuity under Fluid or Porous Matrix.

tools.example:
ht > Porous Medium 1 (LTNE) > Fluid 1 > right-click > Inflow (fluid inlet temperature)
ht > Porous Medium 1 > Porous Matrix 1 > right-click > Heat Flux (heated wall acting on the solid phase)
tools.notes: Heat Source and Initial Values at interface level do not apply on LTNE domains; use the phase subnodes.

tools.name: Lumped System Connector (Heat Transfer)
tools.description: Boundary node that connects a finite-element heat transfer model to a Lumped Thermal System network: the average (or, with Isothermal terminal, the pointwise) boundary temperature is imposed at the node of an External Terminal of the lts interface, and the heat rate computed by the network is applied back on the boundaries. Use it to represent heat sinks, fans or cold plates by thermal resistors instead of geometry.
tools.usage: Physics > Boundaries > Lumped System Connector; select the External Terminal in the Source list.

parameters.name: Source
parameters.description: External Terminal feature of the Lumped Thermal System providing P_ext.

parameters.name: Isothermal terminal
parameters.description: Constrain space-dependent T instead of the boundary average.

tools.notes: Initial temperature of the connector comes from the External Terminal for transient runs. Shell interfaces have edge and interface variants.

tools.name: Harmonic Perturbation (Heat Transfer)
tools.description: Subnode of Temperature and External Temperature (and a right-click option on sources) that defines the harmonic amplitude of a prescribed temperature Delta_T0 around the equilibrium value T0, used only in Frequency-Domain Perturbation (Thermal Perturbation, Frequency Domain) study steps.
tools.usage: Temperature > right-click > Harmonic Perturbation; for sources right-click the Heat Source / Line/Point Heat Source node > Harmonic Perturbation.

parameters.name: Delta T0
parameters.description: Temperature perturbation amplitude (complex values allow a phase).

tools.example:
ht > Temperature 1: T0 = 300[K] > Harmonic Perturbation 1: Delta T0 = 1[K]
Study: Stationary + Frequency-Domain Perturbation, freq = 0.01, 0.1, 1 Hz
tools.notes: Ignored in stationary and time-dependent studies.

tools.name: Thin Rod (Heat Transfer, 3D edges)
tools.description: Edge node that models conductive rods (wires, pins, thermocouples, heat pipes approximated as rods) located on edges of a 3D model with a rod radius and thermal properties, so they need not be meshed as volumes. Subnodes add a Line Heat Source inside the rod, Temperature and Point Heat Flux at end points, and Surface-to-Ambient Radiation at the rod ends.
tools.usage: Physics > Edges > Thin Rod (3D components).

parameters.name: r_l
parameters.description: Rod radius.

parameters.name: k_l, rho_l, Cp_l
parameters.description: Rod conductivity (isotropic to full tensor), density, heat capacity.

parameters.name: Subnodes
parameters.description: Line Heat Source, Temperature (Thin Rod), Point Heat Flux (Thin Rod), Surface-to-Ambient Radiation (Thin Rod).

tools.example:
ht > Thin Rod 1 on the thermocouple wire edges: r_l = 0.1[mm], material Copper
Thin Rod 1 > Temperature (Thin Rod) at the cold junction point: T0 = 273.15[K]
tools.notes: Only in 3D; for 2D slender parts use out-of-plane features.

tools.name: Line and Point Heat Sources on Axis (Heat Transfer, 2D axisymmetric)
tools.description: Sources for 2D axisymmetric components located on the symmetry axis: Line Heat Source on Axis models a source with no thickness along the axis (e.g. a heating wire), and Point Heat Source on Axis a source of no spatial extension on the axis (e.g. a small bead). Settings are the same as Line Heat Source and Point Heat Source, and both can be marked as harmonic perturbations.
tools.usage: 2D axisymmetric: Physics > Edges (on axis) > Line Heat Source on Axis; Physics > Points (on axis) > Point Heat Source on Axis.

parameters.name: Ql / Pl
parameters.description: Line source per length or total heat rate (line source).

parameters.name: P0
parameters.description: Point source power.

parameters.name: Harmonic Perturbation
parameters.description: Mark for frequency-domain perturbation studies.

tools.example:
2D axisymmetric hot-wire (transient line source) method:
ht > Line Heat Source on Axis: Ql = 10[W/m] switched on at t = 0
Probe: temperature at r = 0 versus log(t) to extract conductivity
tools.notes: Point and line sources give singular temperatures at the source; evaluate at a distance. Related Java for off-axis line source: physics("ht").create("lihs1", "LineHeatSource", ...).

tools.name: Thermal Insulation, Edge (Heat Transfer)
tools.description: Edge (3D) or point (2D, 2D axisymmetric) condition that introduces a temperature discontinuity along external edges or points where two or more objects touch only along those entities, so that heat does not flow through the line or point contact. Typical for assemblies touching along edges in radiation or conduction benchmarks.
tools.usage: Physics > Edges > Thermal Insulation, Edge (inse1). Java type: ThermalInsulationEdge

parameters.name: Edge/point selection
parameters.description: External edges/points shared by objects in line contact.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("inse1", "ThermalInsulationEdge", 1);
// Application Library: Heat_Transfer_Module/Verification_Examples/cavity_radiation
tools.notes: Only applicable on exterior edges or points.

tools.name: Thermal Connection (Heat Transfer)
tools.description: Global node that connects two boundary selections (connector 1 and connector 2) through a lumped Conductive thermal resistor (resistance R given directly or from conductivity and geometry: plane, cylindrical or spherical shell, optionally with convective enhancement or optically thick radiation), a Thermal capacitor, or a Lumped thermal system subcircuit. Use it to bridge parts that are not meshed between them (e.g. an air gap or a thermal pad).
tools.usage: Physics > Global > Thermal Connection (thermc1). Java: model.component("comp1").physics("ht").create("thermc1", "ThermalConnection", -1)

parameters.name: connectionType
parameters.description: ConductiveThermalResistor, Thermal capacitor, or LumpedThermalSystem.

parameters.name: resistorType / R
parameters.description: ThermalResistance (R) or geometric properties (geomConfig PlaneShell, ..., A, L, r_i, r_o, k).

parameters.name: convEnhanced / opticallyThickParticipatingMedium
parameters.description: Include natural convection (Nusselt correlation) or Rosseland radiation in the resistor.

tools.notes: For shells, Thermal Connection, Interface-Interface connects interfaces of layered shells.

tools.name: Heat Flux, Interface and Temperature, Interface (Heat Transfer in Shells)
tools.description: Boundary-interface features of the Heat Transfer in Shells interface that apply a heat flux q0 or a prescribed temperature on the exterior interfaces (top/bottom faces) of a shell and, for layered shells, at the interfaces between layers. The interface selection (top, bottom, between layer i and i+1) is made in the Interface Selection section with preview plots of the layer cross section.
tools.usage: Heat Transfer in Shells (htlsh) > Boundaries > Heat Flux, Interface (hfi1) / Temperature, Interface (tempi1). Java types: HeatFluxInterface, TemperatureInterface

parameters.name: Restrict to layered boundaries
parameters.description: Apply only where a layered material is defined.

parameters.name: Interface selection
parameters.description: Top/bottom or internal layer interfaces (applyTo, shelllist).

parameters.name: q0 / T0
parameters.description: Flux (general, convective, heat rate) or temperature value.

tools.notes: Edge-level Heat Flux (lhf) and Temperature (ltemp) nodes act on shell edges instead.

tools.name: Thermal Connection, Interface-Interface (Heat Transfer in Shells)
tools.description: Global feature of the Heat Transfer in Shells interface that connects the interfaces (faces) of two boundary selections of layered shells through a thermal resistor, thermal capacitor or Lumped Thermal System; the selections must use Layer type General and the layered material of the Shell Properties section.
tools.usage: Heat Transfer in Shells > Global > Thermal Connection, Interface-Interface (tcii1). Java type: ThermalConnectionInterfaceInterface

parameters.name: Connector 1 / Connector 2
parameters.description: Boundary selections and the layer interfaces to connect.

parameters.name: connectionType
parameters.description: Conductive thermal resistor, thermal capacitor, or lumped thermal system.

tools.example:
Heat Transfer in Shells > Thermal Connection, Interface-Interface 1: connect top interface of laminate A to bottom interface of laminate B through R = 0.02[K/W]
// Application Library: Heat_Transfer_Module/Tutorials,_Thin_Structure/lumped_composite_thermal_barrier_shells
tools.notes: Domain counterpart: Thermal Connection (ht).
